Author code: h2o_lightning_shim.py (sha256 8af95357658a7258b233a3f8bcea2cb48b0297a145ee2e1fd3957006e3ffcb92, H2O's v1.1 shim with marked [v37] lines), h2o_lightning_shim_v37.py (sha256 b779d907b2a1438a4fad2ced36944368e2c1073dca72d9cd0318f9755140e98e, 368 lines, imports only json, math and pathlib) and serve_config.json (sha256 fc26d64ff050121c159fc0570cfee49560e3e7f3d3df076aa96b944c1aa4a8e3). Stack: the official image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 pinned by digest sha256:8a69ffad015f138d7170c4ddc429e230a3bc1c1719f67e14324749df200a4b90 (the stack of the live H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1 row; no overlay, no pip, no source checkout), with vLLM 0.30.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.17.0, tokenizers 0.23.2, triton 3.7.1 and huggingface-hub 1.32.0 asserted on the node before any weights step, and a first-party Triton compiler gate passed before the weights step and again inside the scored container. Source review (text only; no author file was imported or executed on the evaluator host; line by line over the request path and the delta against H2O's reviewed v1.1 shim): verdict PASS WITH CONDITIONS, no stop condition; no branch on item text, ids, gold labels or item lists; the delta is a small pure-Python readout patch (no I/O, network, subprocess, eval, exec or pickle); no auto_map and no trust_remote_code; weights and tokenizer are safetensors and tokenizer files only. The conditions were binding: author code only on a disposable rented pod, every override variable unset, the model directory exactly the 17 pinned files (no subdirectory, symlink or cache) checked on the node and again inside the scored container, weights fetched on the pod by first-party code at the full revision and sha256-verified, and the served configuration read back from /health. /health was compared with the preregistered configuration by strict dictionary equality in the pre-sealed smoke, in the pre-warm, right after the scored run and after the record-only replay (all equal; the same values each time). The server ran in a read-only, network-none, cap-drop-ALL, no-new-privileges container with no credentials, read-only model and input mounts and private output, after a network-cut proof (only loopback, no default route, DNS and TCP failed) and an offline model-hash proof; the scored process was a fresh server process in a fresh container whose first request was the frozen driver's own public pre-warm. Model: https://huggingface.co/PhillyLabs/philly-decider-v2 at 36e5ddde2c59021d37ed5974aa7c9f16062050e0 (17 files; model.safetensors 8,411,558,400 bytes, sha256 70941015cc8d822bfba82134dd9b86e79e722df4c1be9bc39a8c99755322138e; every file hashed against the pinned list on the node, 17 of 17 verified, and again inside the scored container, 17 of 17), about 4.2 B parameters, BF16, Qwen3_5ForCausalLM, text only, one CUDA device, no quantisation. phillylabs_philly_decider_v2.disclosure: FIRST MEASUREMENT of PhillyLabs/philly-decider-v2 in this intake (submitted by the author through a public GitHub issue). FINE-TUNE OF A FINE-TUNE: the card says Philly Decider v2 is a fine-tune of H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1 by H2O.ai (h2oai/h2o-lightning-4b at 193ad740925b176a3b70a5a13a7cff2f2fadd01e, Apache-2.0, itself a post-train of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B). The author's change is a merged LoRA delta (round-1 adapter plus 0.5 times a round-2b adapter, concatenated rank 256, merged in fp32 with one bf16 rounding) plus changed readout settings; the tokenizer, chat template, prompt format, label tokens, serve.sh and the shim's prompt and trim code are H2O's. The name is 'Jev-compatible' only: it is a Philly Decider model, not a Jev model; the author is PhillyLabs and the base model's author is H2O.ai. Per the release-owner position, a disclosed fine-tune of another entrant's open model is ranked like any fine-tune, with the lineage named on the row. RELATED ROWS: the live H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1 row is a different row and is not replaced; nothing is inferred between the two. The same author's separate philadelphia-decider-4b is a different model; this row says nothing about it. SIBLING CHECK: the model.safetensors LFS sha256 70941015cc8d822bfba82134dd9b86e79e722df4c1be9bc39a8c99755322138e is NEW: it differs from the declared base revision (c65443b1d28891ffc4b6f7d90028c542d6ccb24c2f9cd6a46a8294a44ab0ffae), from all 50 H2O-Lightning-4B revisions, from the author's philadelphia-decider-4b and its base Mapika/decider-4b, and matches no LFS blob of the 173 live JevBench row repositories (171 compared; 2 repositories answered 401 and could not be compared: Uniphore/uniphore-4b-decider and nemotron-deciffusion/Nemotron-Deciffusion-8B-v2). The tokenizer.json is identical to the base's (record only). THE AUTHOR'S OWN SERVING PATH on our rented hardware, run unmodified (see code_revision), with no shim of ours. PROMPT (H2O v1.1's, unchanged): Qwen chat template with thinking off, the system line 'You are a decision engine...', then record, question and options with one label per option (255 labels available), compact JSON for a structured state, and an 'Answer:' prefill; one forward pass per decision, label logprobs only, max_tokens 1, no generated text, no ensemble, no retry. NATIVE OUTPUTS AND READOUT POST-PROCESSING (the author's [v37] readout, served as shipped): choice = softmax((logit + b) / 0.798298) with the position bias b = [0, 0.15, 0.2, -0.15, -0.05, 0, 0, 0] on option positions 1 to 8; noul = softmax(logit / 0.933033) and then H2O's 0.801 floor (a yes/no probability whose larger side is below 0.801 is moved to 0.801 on its own side; the answer never changes; the same device as the live H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1 row, the Calibration axis includes its effect, and we did not measure a variant without it); score = a 'mirror' readout: p = softmax(logit / 0.7), m = the median level of p, served probabilities = (p + p reflected about m) / 2, so the served score is the median level m and does NOT preserve the softmax mean. The configured temperature_by_type.score value 0.5 is never used by the mirror readout (dead setting, disclosed). READOUT FIT, AUTHOR STATEMENT (not independently verified): the author states that these per-type temperatures, the choice position bias and the mirror score readout were fitted on 887 unpublished local calibration rows ('EIKOS-CAL + REALDEV-CAL') and that no JevBench items were used. No rows, fit scripts or fit receipts are published (the repository's MERGE_MANIFEST records the weights lineage only and lists an older serve_config.json hash). Our public-only check found no alignment between the position bias and the public items' answer-position prior (Pearson r 0.00); that is weak evidence only, and the temperatures cannot be checked offline. CONFIGURATION: the shipped settings exactly as in code_revision and /health; no other setting was measured and nothing is inferred about one. TEACHERS (author statement): DeepSeek V4.1-Flash (API, thinking on; target teacher, under the DeepSeek API terms), Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (labels on round-1 error items), and two models that are themselves JevBench entrants: Chon-1.0-12B-Fast (logit teacher where no DeepSeek label exists) and Torchcast-4B v1.2 (a yes/no second vote only, never a target). TRAINING DATA AND CARD NUMBERS (author statements, not independently verified): public decision-style datasets under permissive licences; the card says no JevBench item text and no answers were used for training or model selection and that training rows passed an 8-gram overlap filter against the public items. We did not inspect training examples or verify overlap with JevBench public or sealed items, so contamination of the sealed draw is unchecked. The card's 61.96 versus 57.92 (H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1, stock readout) are measured on the author's own 1,200-item held-out set with the author's scorer; they are not JevBench numbers and are not used here. CONTEXT AND TRIM, SILENT: a state over 32,000 tokens is cut to its first 16,000 tokens, the text '\n...\n' and its last 16,000 tokens before the prompt is built, with no signal in the response; the author's default and the same as the live H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1 row. The 15 trimmed items were counted offline and frozen by the lead before launch as 'trimmed, answered' (count only; expected-outcomes sha256 c2ccee9a2f210a8206808540a5fb52b8ec99c0dfc2eb0b24918018ee012afeb2; counts sha256 df9887809a9f53393aaec208d19ee39007eedf0d82bd9717e46a2cf8c6b109f8; preregistered) and the measured trim record equals the preregistered set exactly: 15 of 15 trimmed, no other item trimmed, no refusal, no unexpected failure. Their answers rest on the first and last 16,000 tokens of the state, not the whole state. The longest original state in the draw is 80,370 tokens; the longest untrimmed prompt is 1,856 tokens and the most options on any item is 9 (limit 255). A prompt of 40,960 tokens or more, or more than 255 options, would be refused with HTTP 422; none occurred (boundary proven on the pod before any sealed item: 40,959 tokens answered, 40,960 and 42,000 refused, 256 options refused, with recovery after each). ANSWERED: 1,500 of 1,500, HTTP 200 on every row, no refusal, no error, no native non-200 status and no deviation record. USAGE: the server-native input usage (1,234,232 tokens over all 1,500 rows, 752,008 on the common 1,485) equals our first-party count exactly, 0 mismatches; output_tokens 0 natively; the unit is the final prompt, so for the 15 trimmed items it is the trimmed prompt (the original states are not billed). HARDWARE AND LATENCY: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96 GB with stock vLLM 0.30.0, so latency is not comparable with the author's own figures on other hardware. 10 s RULE: 0 decisions took 10 s or longer, so no decision is scored wrong under the 10 s rule in the v1.7 share view (the frozen v1.6 and v1.7-off views apply no time limit); measured loopback p95 0.05 s, maximum 1.09 s over all 1,500 requests; scored loop 59 s. The pre-sealed cold first request, a trimmed prompt built from the longest original state, took 1.39 s. The v1.7 share ranking uses the common self-hosted latency estimate (2 times measured p50 plus 0.15 s); this adjustment is an assumption, not a measured hosted endpoint. DETERMINISM (record-only): the first 50 requests were run twice after the scored loop, 50/50 bit-identical, 0 argmax flips, maximum probability difference 0.0. In the pre-sealed smoke, the same body sent twice gave identical answers for all three types; two groups of unique synthetic states that differed only by a tag text gave different probabilities (record-only, not a repeat test). OFFLINE COUNTER: the same counter that produced the sealed counts was run on the public items before the launch (231 answered, 0 trimmed, 150,981 input tokens, at most 6 options) and reproduces byte for byte. PREREGISTRATION AMENDMENT 1 WAS NOT APPEND-ONLY (custody disclosure): it was written before any pod and before any sealed item, closed the findings of an independent review, and says that it supersedes the earlier wording, so the preregistration text was edited in place rather than only appended to. It rewrote the section on the served readout (the mirror readout is now described as setting the score mean to the median level), the cold-probe line (the first POST is a cold trimmed probe at the longest original state, 80,000 changed to 80,370 tokens) and stop rule 8 (a non-200 status returned by the author's server is now passed unchanged to the frozen driver and its own unchanged stop rule instead of stopping the run). Its other fixes: the /health contract value for the readout's median spread (the author's code snaps the default 0.1 to a 2^-20 grid and publishes 0.10000038146972656), a check of the scored process's configuration at completion, and the bound on the cold probe. The counter, rendering, tokenizer pins and the sealed counts were unchanged and not re-counted. Custody noted the edit, accepted it and asked that it be disclosed on the row. A later amendment (RTX PRO 6000 FIN-03 only, A6000 removed after another row's pre-sealed TTL-fit stop) was a pure append to the preregistration; custody confirmed the final kit hash (78487d76) again. The run did not trigger any of the amended stop rules: no native non-200 status, no deviation record and no configuration difference occurred. LICENCE NOTE: weights Apache-2.0 per the model card and the repository's LICENSE file (H2O.ai's licence file kept unchanged; NOTICE lists the author's modifications), ungated; the base h2oai/h2o-lightning-4b is Apache-2.0 and the backbone Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B is Apache-2.0; teacher labels from DeepSeek V4.1-Flash fall under the DeepSeek API terms; the disposition is for the release owner. ATTEMPT HISTORY: one measured attempt. One earlier attempt stopped before any reservation or create call (stock race), so no instance existed and no sealed item reached a model before the measured attempt.
